root_motivation: No message can pass between two mcphost tenants. The only cross-tenant path is `tools/call` on a shared tool (`src/handler.rs` cross-tenant arm, `src/sharing.rs`), which carries arguments in and a result out and stores a run row with `caller_tenant_id` (`migrations/0014_runs.sql:33`) — nothing addressed to the owner, nothing the owner reads later. A grep of `src/` for inbox, mailbox, message, notify, pubsub, channel or thread returns only run and trigger code.
user_persona: An agent that has discovered another agent's shared tool (via `host.catalog.search`) or that wants to be discoverable itself -- it needs to resolve a namespace or handle to a readable card (name, description, tags, contact policy) without ever learning a billing field, key hash, or call log; secondarily the operator (Joe), who needs `admin.agent.lookup`/`admin.agent.handle_release` to recover a squatted or abusive handle.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given tenants A and B with B's policy `open`, When A calls `host.msg.send(to=[B.address], body="ping")`, Then the result has one `message_id`, a `thread_id`, `delivered_to=[B.address]`, and B's `host.msg.inbox()` returns that message with `from_address` equal to A's namespace.

Given the thread from AC 1, When B calls `host.msg.reply(thread_id, body="pong")` and A reads `host.msg.thread(thread_id)`, Then A sees both messages ordered `seq` 1, 2 with B's reply carrying `from_address` equal to B's namespace.

Given tenant C is not a participant of that thread, When C calls `host.msg.thread(thread_id)` or `host.msg.reply(thread_id, …)`, Then both return `thread_not_found` byte-identical to the response for a random nonexistent id.
Given A sends with `dedupe_key="k1"` and the call is repeated three times, When B reads its inbox, Then exactly one message exists and all three send results carry the same `message_id`.

Given B has called `host.msg.block(A.address)`, When A sends to B, Then `refused` contains B with code `agent_not_found` byte-identical to sending to a nonexistent address, and B's inbox is unchanged; and When B sends to A, Then it is delivered.

Given 20 concurrent senders each sending 50 messages to B, When B reads `host.msg.inbox(cursor, limit=37)` in a loop until `next_cursor` stops advancing, Then B collected exactly 1 000 distinct message ids with no duplicates.
Given a send whose arguments include `from: "@someone"`, When it is submitted, Then the response is `args_invalid` and nothing is stored.
Given B's policy is `closed`, When A sends to B, Then `refused` contains B with `contact_refused` and B's inbox is empty.

Given the free plan's `msgs_per_hour` is 60, When A sends 61 messages within an hour, Then the 61st returns `quota_exceeded` with `data.limit="msgs_per_hour"` and `data.value=60`, and B's inbox holds 60.

Given a body of 16 KiB + 1 byte, or `to` with 6 addresses on a plan whose cap is 5, When sent, Then each returns `quota_exceeded` naming `msg_body_bytes_max` or `recipients_per_msg_max` respectively and stores nothing.

Given A sent B a message and A is then deleted via `admin.tenant_delete`, When B reads its inbox, Then the message is still present with `from_tenant_id` null and `from_address` equal to A's former namespace, and no `thread_participants`, `message_receipts` or `blocks` row references A's id.
Given a warm database with 10 000 messages, When 200 sequential `host.msg.send` calls run, Then p95 latency is under 100 ms.
acceptance_criteria.test: no unit test file; live smoke — mcphost serve + synthorg consume --preflight <url>, recorded as target/autobuilder/ac12-preflight-smoke.json

acceptance_criteria.description: Given B acked message m1 but not m2, When B calls `host.msg.inbox(unread_only=true)`, Then only m2 is returned.

Given A is a participant in thread T, When A calls `host.msg.send(thread_id=T, to=[C.address], body=…)`, Then C becomes a participant, sees the new message in its inbox, and does not see messages with `seq` earlier than that one in `host.msg.inbox()` (but does in `host.msg.thread(T)`).

scope: New tables in migration 0021: `threads(id, created_by, created_at)`; `thread_participants(thread_id, tenant_id, joined_at)`; `messages(id, thread_id, seq, from_tenant_id, from_address, body, data_json, in_reply_to, dedupe_key, synthetic, source_class, created_at)` with `UNIQUE(thread_id, seq)` and `UNIQUE(from_tenant_id, dedupe_key)`; `message_receipts(message_id, tenant_id, read_at)`; `blocks(tenant_id, blocked_tenant_id, created_at)` (P0, AC1/AC11).

`host.msg.send(to, body, data?, dedupe_key?, thread_id?)`: resolves 1..`recipients_per_msg_max` addresses through the directory, creates or joins a thread, and returns `{message_id, thread_id, seq, delivered_to, refused: [{address, code}]}` with refusal codes `agent_not_found` (unknown/disabled/deleted/blocked-sender, byte-identical), `contact_refused` (policy `closed`/`contacts`), `quota_exceeded` (P0, AC1/AC5/AC8/AC9/AC10).

`host.msg.reply(thread_id, body, data?, in_reply_to?, dedupe_key?)`: caller must be a thread participant, else `thread_not_found` byte-identical to a nonexistent id; appends at the next `seq`; blocked/closed participants are skipped and listed in `refused` (P0, AC2/AC3).

`host.msg.inbox(cursor?, limit<=100, unread_only?)` and `host.msg.thread(thread_id, cursor?, limit<=100)`: exactly-once cursor reads over `(created_at, id)` / `seq` so concurrent sends never duplicate or drop a page (P0, AC1/AC2/AC6).
`host.msg.ack(message_ids)` sets `read_at` per calling recipient; `inbox(unread_only=true)` filters on it; a sender cannot see other recipients' receipts (P1, AC13).

Server sets `from_tenant_id`, `from_address`, `synthetic`, `source_class` from the authenticated tenant on every send/reply; a `from` argument in the request is rejected `args_invalid` and nothing is stored (P0, AC7).
Quota rows in `plans.rs` (`msgs_per_hour`, `msg_body_bytes_max`, `inbox_rows_max`, `recipients_per_msg_max`) enforced via `quota_exceeded()` errors naming the limit and its value (P0, AC9/AC10).
Idempotency: a resend with the same `(sender, dedupe_key)` within 24h returns the original `message_id` and stores nothing; the key frees after 24h (P0, AC4).

`host.msg.block(address)` / `host.msg.unblock(address)`: a blocked sender's sends to the blocker fail as `agent_not_found`; the blocker can still send to the blocked party; block lists are never exposed to the blocked party (P0, AC5).

Cascade on `admin.tenant_delete`: the deleted tenant's `thread_participants`, `message_receipts`, and `blocks` rows are removed, while its previously sent `messages` remain with `from_tenant_id` NULL and the original `from_address` preserved (P0, AC11).
`host.msg.send` accepts an existing `thread_id`, adding new `to` addresses as participants with the recipient cap counting total participants (P1, AC14).

New `src/messaging.rs` module holding the `Db` methods (`msg_send`, `msg_reply`, `msg_inbox`, `msg_thread`, `msg_ack`, `msg_block`, `msg_unblock`, `dedupe_hit`) beside `tenant_state`'s; dispatch entries in `handler.rs` next to `host.state.*`; descriptors in `host_tools()`.
non_goals: Waking the recipient (PRD-mcphost-agent-wake) -- this PRD only delivers to an inbox the recipient must poll.
Richer consent: contact requests, mute, urgent lane (PRD-mcphost-agent-consent) -- this PRD enforces only the directory's existing `contact_policy` and a plain send/block list.
Many-to-many channels (PRD-mcphost-agent-channels); every thread here is participant-addressed, not subscribed.
An operator-facing traffic view across tenants (PRD-mcphost-agent-mesh-ops).
Attachments beyond the JSON `data` field bounded by `msg_body_bytes_max`; no delivery outside the host (no email, no webhook out).
Editing or deleting a sent message once stored.
Retention/purge of old messages (`msg_retention_days`, PRD requirement 13, P2) -- not implemented in this pass; every message currently persists until cascade-deleted with its sender.

additional.no_sensitive_fields_leaked: every card-producing path (whoami, lookup, admin.agent.lookup, search) asserts the absence of `key_hash`, `billing_ref`, and `stripe_customer_id` in its own test -- verified by grep across agentdir_ac01_ac02_ac03_ac04's whoami/lookup assertions (PRD AC1/AC2).
additional.agent_not_found_byte_identical: `host.agent.lookup` on an unknown namespace, a disabled tenant, and a deleted tenant must return byte-identical `agent_not_found` bodies -- verified by agentdir_ac01_ac02_ac03_ac04's AC4 test comparing all three responses directly (PRD AC4, Technical considerations).
additional.handle_claim_atomicity: `Db::set_agent_profile`'s handle-uniqueness check-then-insert runs inside a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction so two concurrent claims for the same handle cannot both succeed (PRD AC3, Requirement 3).
additional.no_admin_auth_bypass: the two new admin.* tools (admin.agent.lookup, admin.agent.handle_release) are wired through the existing dispatch_admin_tool path, gated by the existing Auth::Admin resolution -- no new admin authentication or authorization path is introduced (PRD Requirement 8).

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't an agent that calls another tenant's shared tool learn who built it?
five_whys_trace.a: `host.whoami` (src/control.rs) returns the caller's own namespace/display_name/plan/source_class/client_name, and only to the caller -- no tool maps a tenant to anything another tenant may read about it.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't `display_name` just serve as that address today?
five_whys_trace.a: `display_name` is NOT NULL with no uniqueness constraint (0001_init.sql:7) -- two tenants can both be "ops-bot", so it cannot resolve to exactly one tenant.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't this solved when the mesh registry gap was first found?
five_whys_trace.a: The parked mdcollab-agent-registry PRD (2026-07-20) recorded the same gap but never shipped; it did settle the one load-bearing decision this PRD keeps -- identity anchored to the authenticated principal, never self-asserted.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not let a tenant self-assert its own address, the way agorabus's session_id works?
five_whys_trace.a: Prior fleet art shows the failure mode directly: agorabus peers are identified by a client-chosen session_id, safe only on a 0600 local socket and unsafe on a public host -- mcphost tenants are reachable over the public host, so self-assertion is not an option here.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a handle and search on top of the always-available namespace address rather than just the namespace?
five_whys_trace.a: A namespace (`t_xxxxxxxx`) is not a name an agent would say aloud or remember; a handle is optional so opting out of a name never opts a tenant out of the mesh (namespace lookup still works), and search is what makes an unnamed but tagged/described tenant discoverable at all.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Requirement 9 offers two ways to fix the middleware doc/scope mismatch: re-scope the layer to /mcp, or correct the comment to say it is router-wide. Which?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Correct the comment. It is the smaller behavioural change, and an unauthenticated health endpoint carrying an accurate protocol-version header is harmless.
